text.p: The following are the leading stories in the Maltese press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Draft law on new system to replace Value Added Tax is expected to be published late on Monday. The government has been having talks with private sector bodies on how the system would be introduced.
- Soldiers arrest man after finding him in possession of quantity of pills, believed to be drugs.

- Moslem group says it will hold Maltese authorities responsible for safety of Libyan refugee, 28-year-old writer Najib Harari, arrested on Friday at Libyan request for alleged involvement in drugs and arms smuggling. Harari had served seven-month prison term for entering Malta on a false passport and was re-arrested as he left for Sweden where according to the group Liberty for the Moslem World he had been granted political asylum.
- Archbishop meets bus drivers during Workers' Day meeting.
- Opposition leader Eddie Fenech Adami holds talks with farmers and tells them they would have benefited from membership of the European Union.
